added_claim_errors: Step 3's maximum omits existing IRA contributions; the later combined Roth-cap warning does not fix the compensation-limited calculation.
“Finish by December 31, 2026 so it counts” incorrectly makes December the federal deadline.
“If you contributed in 2021–2026, that money isn't eligible” wrongly excludes all 2021 contributions; eligibility depends on the exact transfer and contribution dates.
A check paid to the son does not itself create an excess Roth contribution; that requires an IRA deposit exceeding his permitted contributions.
“Which can restart the clock” presents beneficiary-change consequences too definitively; whether the 15-year clock restarts is unresolved.
The source's claimed “updated Aug. 2026” date is unverified from the packet.
“Not every 529 plan has its rollover process running smoothly yet” and “December is a busy month for processors” are unsupported operational claims.

The four-way minimum is wrong when compensation is below $7,500 and other IRA contributions exist: $4,000 compensation and $2,000 contributed yields $4,000 under its formula, but only $2,000 is permitted.
The standalone example “He earns $4,000: $4,000” needs an explicit assumption of no other IRA contributions and sufficient eligible funds.
The specific Form 1099-Q “Box 4b” instruction is not verified by the packet.
“Check both forms in early 2027” assumes reporting availability that the packet does not establish.
“The reporting is cleaner” when both transactions occur in 2026 is an unsupported procedural assertion.

reasons: Both immediately reject the $48,000 rollover and correctly calculate the $13,000 lifetime remainder, but both give an unsafe annual-amount calculation when compensation is limited and other IRA contributions exist. B wins because it avoids A's incorrect December deadline and blanket exclusion of 2021 contributions, although it does not clearly explain plan-dependent processing of a prior-year-designated rollover. Neither states the $40,500 minimum nonqualifying amount or the precise excess-removal deadline and its limited effect on penalties, and B is unnecessarily repetitive. Assessment used only the packet; additional reporting and source-date assertions listed as unverified were not independently checked.
